summary: No new evidence this turn; update.json is submitted as applied, and the one factual point worth stating is a record-hygiene artifact I can now pin down. My previous submission (the source-anchor and scoped-negative pass) was stored correctly as interpretation 4099b8f3cc5c45d2b3c3049ce5a5c0de-interpretation-0 on question 9c549c026d7341f2b1e328826eac6dc3-question-0, and it also added a new source anchor (commit_index_staging, raft.go 1392-1404) plus the tree-wide documentation negative; both are visible in the stored record. But the same submission re-declared the @restart_config investigation block, and the controller materialised that as a second root question node rather than updating the existing one: state.json now holds investigations[4] with id 4099b8f3cc5c45d2b3c3049ce5a5c0de-question-0, version 1, parent_id null, the same question text as the original node, the enriched source list including commit_index_staging, and no interpretation attached — while interpretations[72] still carries investigation_id 9c549c026d7341f2b1e328826eac6dc3-question-0. The controller's own references map now resolves @restart_config to the new id, so the two nodes describe one question, and my reading is that this split is an artifact of re-submitting an investigation for an already-established question, not a research result and not a change in any conclusion. I deliberately did not repoint the interpretation at the new node, because that would detach it from the question whose history and earlier interpretations live under 9c549c..., and the remaining seconds of this allocation are not a safe window for a structural edit; flagging the two ids and the exact mismatch is the honest handoff. The finding itself is unchanged and stays as validated: the trigger is the persisted commit index at or above the newest configuration entry (receipts 656e33fb90f24c58a94928eeeeb938aa and 202311f4911e4af5828d49134f37811c), with the empty-configuration, stale-membership, resurrected-voter, forgotten-added-voter, client-contract and operator-recovery consequences each receipt-backed with controls and repeats, and the two known blemishes (the earlier over-broad repair claim, the stored repair Fact's shortened evidence list) documented rather than rewritten.
